Effect sizes of binary variables on continuous scores

Source: R/binary_effects.R
cor_binary_effects.Rd

For a binary variable (e.g. a biomarker "high" vs "low"), the correlation is bounded by the split between groups and is not comparable with the correlation of a continuous variable (see cor_binary_note()). This function returns what to report instead, with existing tests:

  • difference in means M_1 - M_0 and its CI: stats::t.test() with equal variances (the test of the point-biserial r);

  • rank-biserial correlation r_rb = 2U / (n_0 n_1) - 1 = P(Y_1 > Y_0) - P(Y_1 < Y_0) = 2 AUC - 1 (Kerby 2014), with U the Mann-Whitney statistic of stats::wilcox.test(); CI from effectsize::rank_biserial() if installed;

  • for comparison, the observed r_s and r_pb and the bound sqrt(3pq) of |r_s|.

Usage

cor_binary_effects(data, bin_vars, y_vars, labels = NULL, ci = 0.95)

Arguments

data

data frame

bin_vars

binary variables (non-binary ones are dropped with a warning)

y_vars

continuous outcomes

labels

named vector variable -> display label (kept for the tables)

ci

confidence level

Value

tibble, one row per (binary variable, score): X, Y, level0, level1, n0, n1, prop1, mean0, sd0, mean1, sd1, median0, median1, diff, diff_low, diff_high, p_t, r_rb, r_rb_low, r_rb_high, p_mw, r_s, r_s_bound, r_pb.

Details

Group 1 = upper level of the binary variable (as in as_cor_numeric()). p-values are raw.

References

Kerby DS (2014). Comprehensive Psychology 3:11.IT.3.1. doi:10.2466/11.IT.3.1

Examples

d <- simulate_cor_data(150)
cor_binary_effects(d, c("BIN_CRP", "BIN_IL6"), c("depression", "fatigue"))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 24
#>   X       Y      level0 level1    n0    n1 prop1 mean0   sd0 mean1   sd1 median0
#>   <chr>   <chr>  <chr>  <chr>  <int> <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>

#> 2 BIN_CRP fatig… low    high      73    69 0.486  8.02  3.51  8.61  3.69     8.7
#> 3 BIN_IL6 depre… low    high     115    27 0.190 11.8   3.31 13.8   2.80    12  
#> 4 BIN_IL6 fatig… low    high     115    28 0.196  7.61  3.42 10.3   3.07     8  
#> # ℹ 12 more variables: median1 <dbl>, diff <dbl>, diff_low <dbl>,
